names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 5 martie, «Sfântul Cuvios Marcu Pustnicul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Μαρτίου, «Όσιος Μάρκος ο ασκητής και Θαυματουργός», with the rank word and the epithets left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's fourth heading for the Julian 5 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Преподобни Марко Подвижник.“, with the rank word Преподобни left off. Подвижник, the ascetic, is kept rather than stripped as a second rank: it is the by-name this folder's English name already carries from the other two calendars, which print «Marcu Pustnicul» and «Μάρκος ο ασκητής», and the bare forename would fold with the corpus's other men of the name.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 5 марта ст. ст., name page 1463, «Марк Нитрийский, Египетский, Келлийский, Постник», with the one rank word left off. The line itself declines the name and gives only Постника, the faster. All three toponymics are kept because all three are part of the name the index carries, **and the index has one more than the life does**: the life page is titled «Марк Нитрийский, Египетский, Постник», without Келлийский. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form, and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts no fold for it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 марта ст. ст. — «Прп. Марка Постника (V)»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 5 martie — «Sfântul Cuvios Marcu Pustnicul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 5ης Μαρτίου — «Όσιος Μάρκος ο ασκητής και Θαυματουργός»

attestations.note: The page says he was an Athenian who lived in the fourth century, left Athens for Antioch and was a disciple of John Chrysostom, whose memory it puts on 13 November; it tells the hyena whose blind cub he healed and which brought him a ram's skin in return, which he would not take until the beast promised to stop harming the sheep of the poor; it says the presbyter of the monastery declared that he had never given him Holy Communion, but that an angel's hand supplied it; and it prints four of his sayings and the tag «Πάντα πώλησαν καὶ Μᾶρκον ἀγόρασαν». No date is written into this folder from it, because the same Greek day carries a second page, «Όσιος Μάρκος ο Αθηναίος», which says of that one «Ίσως να είναι το ίδιο πρόσωπο με τον όσιο Μάρκο τον Ασκητή» — perhaps he is the same person as Mark the Ascetic — and «Συγκεχυμένες και ασαφείς οι πληροφορίες», that the information is confused and unclear; so the Athenian birth and the century cannot be assigned with confidence to one of the two. No hymn is taken either: the whole hymn block on this page is the other Mark's service, word for word the same as the block on the Athenian's page, naming Athens and the abba Serapion who found him in the desert and buried him — neither of which belongs to the life this page tells.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.03.2026 (5. март ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Марко Подвижник.“

attestations.note: The day's fourth and last entry. It gives no year and no century — the forty years before the tonsure and the sixty after it are counted from nothing — so the folder's empty `dates` is unchanged and nothing was inferred from the death of the teacher it names. The entry names the patriarch Photius as having praised his homilies, which is the kind of row this corpus already keeps: `troadius` relates to `nicodemus-the-hagiorite` for the same reason, a later father cited about an earlier one.

hymns.text: Locuitor pustiului, înger în trup și de minuni făcător te-ai arătat, purtătorule de Dumnezeu, Părintele nostru Marcu. Cu postul, cu privegherea și prin rugăciune primind daruri cerești, tămăduiești pe cei bolnavi și sufletele celor ce aleargă la tine cu credință. Slavă Celui Ce ți-a dat ție putere; Slavă Celui Ce te-a încununat pe tine; Slavă Celui Ce lucrează prin tine tuturor tămăduiri.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Marcu Pustnicul

english.text: A dweller of the desert, an angel in the body and a worker of wonders wast thou shown to be, our God-bearing father Mark. By fasting, by vigil and by prayer thou didst receive heavenly gifts, and thou healest the sick and the souls of those who run to thee in faith. Glory to him who gave thee strength; glory to him who crowned thee; glory to him who works healings for all through thee.

floruit.note: The first century any source read gives him, and it is given twice over: days.pravoslavie.ru closes its line for 5 марта ст. ст. with (V) and opens its life «Преподобный Марк подвизался в V веке в Нитрийской пустыне». doxologia.ro, saint.gr and the Охридски пролог give no year and no century, so this folder had no dates at all until now. It is recorded as a floruit and not as a death because the calendar dates his ascetic life and not his end.
